title: unified-rollouts: enhance canary + shadow autorollback safety and observability
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Improve safety and observability for unified rollouts by making canary and shadow autorollback more robust in noisy telemetry environments. Several customers hit transient metric spikes during staged canaries which caused premature rollbacks. This PR adds hysteresis, quorumed metric evaluation, quarantine stage, stronger traceability for decisioning, and manual override hooks.

Summary of changes: 1) Quorumed metrics: autorollback now evaluates a quorum across multiple telemetry sources (latency p95, error-rate, model-quality regressions) before triggering quarantine/rollback. 2) Hysteresis + decay: implement time-decay and minimum sustained window to avoid flipping on short spikes. 3) Quarantine stage: when triggers are borderline we move the rollout into a quarantine probing stage that throttles traffic and runs additional probes before deciding. 4) Observability: emit rollout_decision_reason and per-metric timeline traces to make postmortems and dashboards actionable. 5) Manual recovery + override: add a safe manual-approve API for canary recovery and a kill-switch for admins. 6) Tests & e2e: add unit tests for the quorum algorithm and e2e tests that validate quarantine-to-rollback and quarantine-to-continue transitions. 7) Docs: update rollout docs with new safety model and recommended thresholds.

Why this approach: previous autorollback was single-metric thresholded, which reacted to transient noisy telemetry. Using quorum + hysteresis reduces false positives while quarantine gives operators an automated observation window. Emitting structured decision traces reduces time-to-resolution.

Rollout plan: merged to main behind feature-flag rollout.autorollback.v2. We will enable for 10% of accounts for 48h, monitor rollout_decision_reason, and then increase to 100% if stable. Have a manual rollback runbook and on-call briefing.

Related: ENG-3410 (autorollback improvements backlog), ENG-3382 (post-incident remediation for canary flips), SUP-1428 (customer report referencing SLO blips).

Ethan Brooks (review) - Observability payloads look good; validate that rollout_decision_reason size is bounded. Could we cap history length?

release_notes: Enhance autorollback safety: quorumed metric evaluation, quarantine probing stage, hysteresis windows, manual override API, and improved rollout decision tracing. Safe rollout behind feature flag rollout.autorollback.v2.
release_plan: Enable on 10% accounts for 48h -> monitor rollout_decision_reason and dashboards -> increase to 50% -> 100% if stable. Runbook available in docs/rollouts/autorollback.md
tests_added: Unit tests for quorum evaluator; e2e tests for quarantine transitions and stability guards; added regression test for metric decay/hysteresis.
notes_for_oncall: If rollout_decision_reason contains 'quarantine:probe-failures' and traffic remains throttled, follow quarantine runbook: inspect per-metric timelines, escalate if model-quality regressions persist. Manual override available via admin API with audit log. Contact author Maya Chen or Arjun Patel.
audit_trail: decision traces emitted to traces/rollouts and metrics.rollouts.decision_count with tags (policy, tenant, canary_id)
back_compat: no breaking API changes; added admin endpoint guarded by RBAC. Default behavior unchanged unless feature flag enabled.
additional_context: This PR is a follow-up to the incident on 2026-01-29 where a transient downstream overload caused multiple canaries to flip. It implements the agreed safety model from postmortem ENG-3382.

security_considerations: Admin manual override requires appropriate RBAC permission; audit logs emitted for all manual actions. No secret material introduced.
qa_signoff: QA validated quarantine transitions and rollback gating for both weighted canary and shadow flows.
